record.title: Reflow-soldered surface-mount joint — a board's edge pads onto a carrier's LDS antenna feeds
record.why: halo's mechanical lane owns the board OUTLINE and the four feed positions around its rim, and those are measured. Whether an LDS surface takes reflow solder reliably at this pitch is a process question nobody here has tested, and the pad geometry itself is the electronics lane's. Nothing is claimed.

joins.b: laser-direct-structured feed pads on a moulded carrier

record.standard: IPC-A-610 / J-STD-001 — NOT fetched, CANNOT DETERMINE
record.adds_parts_why: this joint consumes no part; it joins two. No fastener, and deliberately so — a screw would cost 1.5-2.5 mm of a 7.98 mm budget and put metal inside Apple's Ø37.31 antenna keep-out (DECISIONS.md D13).
record.standard_why: Both are paid IPC documents and no copy is on this disk, so no acceptance figure — fillet height, wetting angle, void fraction — is recorded here and compat.py grades none. This is halo's own local record of the same connection KIND that ce-workshop/ce-connections/solder-smt describes; it exists because ce-designs/halo is its own triad root and a dangling ref is a FAIL.
